question: Compare recursion and iteration in programming, highlighting trade-offs in memory and execution.
model_answer: Recursion solves problems by having a function call itself on smaller subproblems until reaching a base case, utilizing the call stack which consumes memory (risking stack overflow). Iteration uses explicit loop constructs (for/while) with a constant memory footprint (O(1) extra space), generally offering better execution performance and less overhead.

Each recursive frame is pushed onto the call stack, requiring O(N) memory and risking a stack overflow. In contrast, iteration repeats code via for or while loops using constant O(1) auxiliary space, avoiding stack overhead.
